title.narrative: Supporting Ground Water Studies in Nigeria

description.narrative: Groundwater is widely used in the Nigeria because it brings large economic benefits per unit volume, it is locally available, drought resilient and has quality requiring minimal treatment. The reliable supply of groundwater, uniform quality and temperature, relative turbidity and pollution free, minimal evaporation losses, and low cost of development are attributes which make groundwater more attractive when compared to other sources. There is need to therefore need to study this important resource with a view of providing the necessary scientific information for policy and discission making, planning and sustainable management. The workplan comprise two activities. 1) Groundwater quality assessment: to commission comprehensive study to assess the quality of groundwater in selected zones/states of the country. With a view of understating the pollutants, the possible sources, fate and transport. 2) Groundwater depletion study: to Investigate the rate of groundwater depletion (in the face of climate change) in specific zones/sates and/or aquifers in the country. This will involve analyzing historical well data and groundwater level measurements to determine long-term trends and assess the sustainability of current extraction practices. Additionally, alternative water management strategies can be explored, such as artificial recharge techniques or water conservation measures, to mitigate the depletion and ensure long-term water availability. The workplan contributes to Aspiration 1, (A Prosperous Africa, based on Inclusive Growth and Sustainable Development) Goal 7 (Environmentally sustainable and climate resilient economies and communities), Priority Area 15 – (Water Security). The workplan also contributes to SDG targets 1.5, 5.1, 6.1, 6.2, 6.2, 6.B. 11.5. 11.6, 13.1, 13.2. The Workplan contribute to outputs 4.5 and 5.2 of the UNESCO-IHP IX Strategic Plan (2022-2029)
